ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher for SGD 2.73 to the rider (unexempt detour mileage only; the metered waiting charge of $0.11 stands under RD-3(c)) and remind the driver that the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct obligation applies unless a route change is agreed before leaving the optimal route.
ruling.reasoning:
Case is a RydeTAXI route-deviation dispute, so RD-2's metered branch applies: only unexempt detour mileage is refunded, at extra_km × (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km).

RD-1 / segmentation: F3 identifies one off-route segment (14:28–14:34, 3.07 km driven vs 1.12 km optimal, +1.94 km, max 786 m from the optimal route). Total excess is +2.2 km [F1] and $3.06 [F4]; the difference of ~0.23–0.26 km is corridor wobble / map-matching noise not attributed to any segment and is not refundable under RD-2.

RD-5 consent (the contested element): the rider's agreement must predate the segment, and its scope is read from the words. The route change was raised at 14:30 [F8] while the segment had already begun at 14:28 [F3], and the rider's "Sure, no problem" came at 14:31 [F9]. The rider's own account ("only mentioned the different route after he had already turned off") matches the timestamps, so the consent is consent-after-the-fact: ground = consent_after_or_none → the segment counts. The driver's post-trip statement that he told the rider beforehand [F11] is a claim, not consent, and is overridden by the timestamped chat/timeline records. On scope alone, even a prior agreement to "go round via Clementi Road" would need a record tying the driven segment to Clementi Road (RD-5/G13); nothing does.

RD-4 not available: F15 records no traffic incident near the route, so no incident exemption; the AYE speed band 2 during 14:10–14:28 [F12] is the only supporting hint, but it is a traffic-band fact that under RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on its own in the MVP, and the band window ends at 14:28, before the detour segment runs its course. No exemption.

RD-2 arithmetic (RydeTAXI, metered): per-km rate = $14.95 ÷ 10.60 km = $1.4104/km [F4, F7]. Refund = 1.94 km × $1.4104/km = $2.7362 → $2.74. Recomputing exactly from the segment's excess ($3.06 − 0.23 km × $1.4104 = $2.7356) gives $2.74 as well; stated as $2.74 for an unexempt segment of 1.94 km. Waiting fee $0.11 [F5] is metered waiting time and is not refundable under RD-3(c); ERP/toll and other add-ons are within published items (FARE-1), and no surge applies [F6].

RD-6 / flag: the driver has 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but of the route category: 0 [F18], so the "repeated route deviation" condition (RD-6) is not met and no account flag is added. Profile facts were not used to decide the case.

Safety screen: all chat messages, the complaint and the driver statement were read — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation (SAFE-1/SAFE-2). safety_concern = none; no escalation.

Evidence status: sufficient — the GPS segment timing, the timestamped chat and the fare breakdown settle every element; evidence_gap = null.

segment_findings.reason: The off-route segment runs 14:28–14:34 [F3], but the driver's route-change message is 14:30 [F8] and the rider's 'Sure, no problem' is 14:31 [F9] — after the deviation had already begun. RD-5 requires the rider's own message to predate the segment's start; the driver's post-trip statement of a prior verbal notice [F11] is not consent. Consent was after the fact, so the +1.94 km of this segment is unexempt under RD-1 and refunded under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that he told the rider in advance; a driver's claim of verbal agreement is not consent (G11) and the timestamped chat [F8, F9] shows the notice came after the segment began at 14:28 [F3].
AYE speed band 2 is a traffic-band fact only; RD-4(b) does not allow a band alone to exempt a segment, and its 14:10–14:28 window predates/does not cover the detour. No traffic incident exists [F15].
